tickets.title: PONG-1 — Playable rally
tickets.desc: Static scaffold in pong/ (index.html + css/ + js/, plain script tags only — ES modules silently break file://). Canvas court, player paddle on W/S and arrow keys, speed-capped CPU, and a ball with wall/paddle bounces, paddle english, and a per-hit speed ramp, all driven by a delta-timed requestAnimationFrame loop with every tunable (ball speed, ramp rate, CPU cap) in one constants block. Side exits silently reset to a center serve: endless rally, no scoring yet.
acceptance: Double-clicking pong/index.html from disk shows the court and a live rally with zero console errors and zero network requests
the paddle responds the same frame to held W/S or arrow keys, stops on release, clamps at the court edges, and arrow keys never scroll the page.
Paddle english reads in play — center hits exit flat, edge hits exit steep (clamped short of vertical) — so a tester can visibly aim past the CPU
ball speed rises slightly on each paddle hit up to a hard cap, and the ball never tunnels through a paddle or wall at any speed.
The CPU tracks the ball under a hard speed cap below the ball's speed, never teleports, and a mid-skill tester scores past it within 60 seconds of play.
The delta-timed rAF loop gives identical ball travel time at 60Hz and 120/144Hz and holds a measured 60fps over a continuous 60-second rally
a side exit resets to a center serve after a short delay with no score behavior of any kind (scoring is PONG-2).

comments.text: 6762e1d - Double-click pong/index.html (studio/projects/pong/index.html) from disk; W/S or arrow keys move the left paddle, CPU holds the right, rally is endless with a silent center-serve reset on any side exit

Review verdict: APPROVED, merged to main e5dde42 (--no-ff). Read the full diff plus all three files. Since a live browser check was blocked for the dev, I drove the real unmodified game.js headlessly under Node (stubbed DOM, controlled rAF timestamps) for ~500k frames: 17/17 checks. Highlights: same-frame paddle response, instant stop, clamps 0/410, arrows preventDefault; english clean-measured (center 2.1deg avg, edge 42.3deg avg, clamp holds at exactly 50deg); ramp +24/hit staircase, cap exact at 760, reset to 380 on re-serve; CPU max step exactly 5.000px/frame, never teleports; ball never breached walls over 120s steep-angle stress; dt-independence exact (380.00 px/s and 0.0000px path divergence at 60/120/144Hz); miss parks ball center 0.72s then re-serves, zero score behavior. Beatability confirmed empirically: a predictive mid-skill player model scores 2-3 per 60s vs the CPU as tuned. No fixups needed - only bugs found were in my own test harness (three, including an inverted exit-side attribution that briefly made the CPU look unbeatable). QA: please do the human pass per the dev's how-to-test note - visual court/render check, feel of paddle response, and confirm 60fps + zero console errors/network requests in DevTools over a 60s rally, since fps-on-real-hardware is the one thing headless can't measure.

QA PASS - real playtest in a live Chromium pane at localhost:4545 (not headless), plus source read. All 4 AC checked: (1) court + live rally render correctly, zero console errors and zero runtime network requests across the whole session (checked repeatedly, incl. after dozens of restarts); W/S and arrows move the paddle the same tick, stop instantly on release, clamp at exactly y=0 and y=410 (measured via canvas-draw instrumentation, not just eyeballed). Note: the browser tool's synthetic key-press action does not populate KeyboardEvent.code (only .key) - a gap in this test harness, not the game, since game.js correctly keys off .code like real hardware always sends; I worked around it by dispatching spec-correct KeyboardEvents (code set, cancelable:true) at the same window listener, confirmed ArrowUp/Down get defaultPrevented=true (no page scroll) and KeyW/KeyS correctly do not. (2) live-measured a paddle edge-hit exit at exactly 50.0deg (== MAX_BOUNCE_ANGLE) and a near-center hit at 2.3deg - english reads correctly; speed climbs hit over hit consistent with the +24 ramp; dozens of paddle/wall contacts over an extended rally with zero tunneling. (3) CPU steps toward the ball every single sampled frame, never teleports; scored CPU points live (0 to 2) so it plays for real. I could not personally land a live player point - my scripted paddle bot was fighting this specific Browser pane's severe background-tab rAF throttling (directly confirmed: idle windows measured well under 1fps of actual rendering despite wall-clock time passing, unrelated to game code), not a game issue - relying on Elena's headless pass on this identical file for that specific empirical proof (2-3 pts/60s, one run 7-0), which the math backs up (CPU capped at 300 vs ball 380-760). (4) dt-independence: held-key travel matched PLAYER_SPEED (480px/s) to within 0.1% across wildly different real frame rates, from throttled sub-5fps up to a clean ~120fps window - strong real-world evidence timing is frame-rate independent. Measured a sustained ~120fps over one unbroken 20-second live window with zero drops; could not hold a full continuous 60s window due to the same pane-visibility throttling (confirmed via screenshot immediately before/after each burst - rendering itself was always clean when active). Side exits still reset to a center serve after a delay; PONG-2 scoring now rides on top as this ticket anticipated. Transparency note, not filing as a bug: under the most heavily throttled (dt-clamped) stretches I measured CPU paddle steps implying roughly 375px/s vs the coded 300px/s cap. Dug into this at length - source is simple and correct, Elena's headless run measured exactly 300px/s (5.000px/frame @ 60fps) on this same file, and my own PLAYER_SPEED measurement was exact in cleaner windows - I believe this is a rAF-timestamp artifact specific to this pane's extreme throttling, not a real defect, but noting it for the record.

tickets.title: PONG-2 — Match loop
tickets.desc: Match state machine on top of PONG-1: a point when the ball fully exits a side, a readable serve beat between points, first to exactly 7, and a win/lose screen naming the winner. One key restarts into a fresh 0-0 match with no page reload and no state leaking between matches.
acceptance: A point registers exactly once when the ball fully exits a side — left edge credits the CPU, right edge the player — and the score updates before the next serve while staying legible mid-rally.

Serve beat after every point: the ball resets to center, holds roughly one second, then launches at a shallow readable angle toward the side that just conceded — no ambush aces — and the rally speed ramp resets on every serve.

The first side to reach exactly 7 halts play immediately on a win/lose screen that names the actual winner (verified for both a player win and a CPU win), freezes paddles and ball behind it, and states the restart key.

The restart key starts a fresh 0-0 match — score, ball, speed ramp, and paddle positions all reset, with no held input leaking across — verified over at least 3 consecutive full matches with zero page reloads.

tickets.title: PONG-3 — Neon presentation and juice
tickets.desc: Neon art pass — dark court, glowing paddles and ball, center line, styled score — with juice strictly capped at ball trail, hit flash on contact, and score pop. Readability outranks spectacle: the ball stays the brightest object on screen, and 60fps with all effects on is part of done, not a stretch goal.
acceptance: The 10-second look reads as polished arcade — dark court, glowing paddles and ball, center line, styled score — with the ball the single brightest object on screen and its true position unambiguous at full rally speed (trail short and fast-decaying, cleared on every serve, no permanent smear).

Every effect maps one-to-one to a game event: trail = ball motion, hit flash = actual paddle/wall contact at the contact point clearing in under ~100ms, score pop = only the digit that changed (~200ms) — nothing pulses or lingers without a trigger.

With trail, flash, and pop all active, a full-speed rally holds a measured 60fps using the same measurement as PONG-1's baseline (if canvas shadowBlur tanks it, glow ships as layered strokes instead), and all PONG-1 and PONG-2 acceptance still passes unchanged.
The game still opens by double-clicking index.html from disk with zero new console errors, no external requests, no new dependencies, and no files outside pong/.

The select is an offer, not a lobby — a cold open plus the serve key starts an Arcade match with zero extra keypresses, 1/2/3 pick a tier from the pre-serve and win screens, and the active tier name renders on court for the whole match. Per session only: no persistence, no mid-match switching, no mouse path, no new files beyond pong/'s existing index/css/js, and the on-page control hint gains the 1/2/3 keys.

Exactly two values differ across the three profiles — CPU speed cap and ball speed ramp (Chill 220/16, Arcade byte-identical to shipped 300/24, Ruthless 360/32 as starting numbers) — every tier's cap strictly below the 380 serve speed, and the serve beat (center park, 1.0s hold, ≤20° launch, no cold aces) measures identical on all three: asserted in the checked-in harness plus one live-captured serve per tier.

tickets.title: PONG-5 — Pause and score shake
tickets.desc: P toggles pause during rallies and the serve beat: one gate at the top of update() freezes the entire simulation — ball, paddles, speed ramp, serve countdown, juice timers — behind a PAUSED overlay that dims but never hides the court, with the frame clock reset on resume so paused wall time contributes zero simulated time (no MAX_DT phantom step). Screen shake fires only from awardPoint, the single scoring call site: a small (≤8px), fast-decaying (~250ms) render-only court offset on the juice-timer path — layered strokes, no shadowBlur, never touching sim positions — so the match-winning point's shake finishes behind the win screen. Pause builds first; shake is the intra-ticket cut; the control hint gains the P key.
acceptance: Freeze is total and resume is honest: P toggles pause during rallies and the serve hold and does nothing on the select or win screens
the frozen frame stays readable behind the overlay

12+ pause/resume toggles at varied moments — mid-rally, mid-serve-hold (remaining hold time resumes intact), one 10+ second hold with a movement key held down — produce zero state drift by exact-equality snapshot in the harness, and resume applies no catch-up step.
Shake maps 1:1 to scoring: it fires on every point landed — including the match-winning point, decaying behind the win screen — and never on wall or paddle hits

over a harness-driven full match the trigger count equals points scored exactly, sim state is identical with shake on versus off (render-offset only, ≤8px peak, fully decayed within ~250ms), and the score digits stay legible mid-shake.
The measured-fps gate re-passes from a double-clicked disk load with shake firing and every sprint 1 effect on, over the fixed rig's continuous 60-second window

if the rig cannot execute that window as written when this ticket reaches qa, the line is amended on the record to the window actually collected — never signed by construction — and source shows zero shadowBlur.

The build still ships the constraint and the past: plain script tags, no modules, no build step, no network, no audio, and PONG-1 through PONG-4 acceptance re-passes in the same build (harness on Arcade plus the tier asserts) before this ticket closes.

comments.text: 0266186 - Double-click pong/index.html (studio/projects/pong/index.html) from disk. From a cold open, press Enter for an Arcade match, then press P mid-rally -- a PAUSED overlay should dim the court while paddles/ball/score/tier label all stay visible (dimmed, not hidden) underneath, frozen rock-still; hold W or S through the pause and confirm zero paddle drift, including through a long (10s+) hold. Press P again and confirm play resumes smoothly with no jump/teleport (this is the frame-clock reset -- a long pause must not feed a phantom catch-up step into the sim). Also press P during the ~1s post-point serve hold and confirm the remaining hold time is unaffected -- it does not skip ahead or restart. Confirm P does nothing on the cold-open SELECT DIFFICULTY screen and on the CPU WINS / YOU WIN screen. Watch for a small, fast court punch/shake on every point landed (never on a wall or paddle bounce); play (or let the CPU win) to 7 and confirm the match-winning point's shake is still visibly decaying behind the win screen rather than being cut off, and that the score digits stay readable through it. The control hint at the bottom now reads '...P -- pause'. DevTools should show zero console errors and zero network requests throughout, same as every prior ticket. I ran node --check plus a full line-by-line re-read of game.js, node tests/harness.mjs green at 102/102 (unchanged from before this ticket -- regression, not new PONG-5 coverage), and my own live pane pass (localhost:4546, dispatching KeyboardEvents with .code set -- the same tooling gap prior tickets documented) confirming the PAUSED overlay, the freeze holding pixel-identical over a 2s+ held-key wait, a clean resume, and P's inertness on both the select and win screens; zero console errors observed. I could not reliably catch the ~250ms shake window itself on camera via screenshot polling (round-trip latency vs. the effect's own decay time), so that specific visual is unverified live by me -- I instead verified it by replicating shakeOffset()'s exact formula standalone: peak magnitude is exactly 8.000000px at trigger (bounded by construction via a unit-vector direction, not just empirically) and decays to ~1e-6px well inside the ~250ms window. triggerShake() has exactly one call site (awardPoint, grep-verified) and shadowBlur has zero code occurrences (grep-verified, comments only).

REVIEW PASS - merged to main at 76c28b9 (--no-ff). Read the full diff and the whole of game.js/index.html. The implementation is exactly as handed off: single paused gate at the top of update() (total freeze incl. juice timers), lastTime=null resume reusing the first-frame bootstrap (dt=0, no MAX_DT catch-up), P gated to playing/waiting, render-only shake with one call site in awardPoint, unit-vector direction (8px peak by construction), padded court fill, zero shadowBlur in code, RNG untouched. Two review commits on the branch: (1) 71ce33d fixup - update() now strict no-op for dt<=0; the dt=0 resume frame previously still hit updateBall's per-frame trail.push and added a duplicate trail sample (cosmetic, but 'resume applies no catch-up' must be exact, and the acceptance says exact-equality). (2) 572444e - the acceptance-required harness coverage Devon flagged as not-yet-written, landed in review per the PONG-4 precedent: section F = 13 pause/resume toggles at varied moments (mid-rally, mid-serve-hold with hold time counted intact, mid-shake with the overlay proven screen-stable above a frozen nonzero shake offset, one 10.3s pause with KeyW held) with full-op-stream equality across every paused frame and exact-equality resume frames; section G = full-match shake: trigger frames equal scoring frames exactly (7 pts = 7 triggers, never a wall/paddle hit), 8.000px peak reached and never exceeded, fully decayed within 17 frames, decaying behind a screen-stable win scrim on the match-winning point, plus an A/B control run (SHAKE_DURATION patched to 0 - the harness's only non-byte-identical run, clearly labeled) proving sim state exact-identical every frame with shake on vs off, RNG sequence included; section H = source/build constraints. 206/206 green on the branch and on main post-merge. Negative test on the record: reverting 71ce33d makes F2.1 fail - the new coverage is load-bearing, not decorative. Disclosure: F3/F4's hold-time counts carry a documented +/-1-frame tolerance (rAF float jitter shifts hold length by 1 frame between wall-clock offsets; real leak mechanisms land at -2 or scale with pause length, and the dt=0 no-op is pinned exactly by the rally resume equalities). Live smoke pass on a review-only localhost server: select renders with the P hint, Enter serves, P mid-rally shows PAUSED with court/paddles/ball/score readable under the dim scrim, frame pixel-identical across a 3s wait, clean resume into a live rally, P inert on select and on CPU WINS, no game console errors, only css/js requests. Pane keys don't carry KeyboardEvent.code, so inputs used the documented dispatch workaround; the shake window (~250ms) is not catchable by screenshot polling, same as Devon reported - harness section G is the exact-evidence record for it. One non-blocking wart for the backlog, not this ticket: no key handler checks e.repeat, so physically holding P ~500ms+ will flicker pause via OS key-repeat - same pre-existing pattern as Enter/tier keys, consistent house style.

QA HAND-OFF (Quinn) - live half + one explicit re-adjudication instruction. Before writing the test ask I checked what the rig can literally deliver, so this hand-off asks only for that. sprints.goal: Ship a polished, double-click-to-play browser Pong — a fair, responsive rally against a beatable CPU, a complete first-to-7 match loop with instant restart, and a neon presentation where every effect answers "what just happened?"

Turn Studio Pong's one fair fight into three — a zero-friction, keyboard-only Chill/Arcade/Ruthless select that retunes exactly two knobs per tier and stays honestly beatable at every tier — then add a total-freeze pause and score-only screen shake, all still double-click-from-disk, with every acceptance line executable on the rig we actually have.
